subjectLine: What the newest Gwinnett numbers tell us
previewText: Fresh Gwinnett market data, a safer July Fourth checklist, and a Saturday stop in Suwanee.

paragraphs: July is here, and the long holiday weekend is just a few days away.
Whether your plans include a cookout, fireworks, a little time around town, or simply enjoying the air conditioning, I hope you have a safe and relaxing Fourth of July.
This week's note includes the newest public Gwinnett housing numbers, a quick holiday safety check, and a local Saturday-morning event.
As always, if you are wondering what the market means for your own home or plans, I am happy to help you sort through it.

market.title: More homes are available, while activity remains steady
paragraphs: Realtor.com reported 3,408 active listings in Gwinnett County during May 2026, up about 11.2% from May 2025. New listings were up about 1.1%, and pending listings were up about 1.8%.

That combination suggests buyers have more choices even though the flow of new listings and pending activity remains close to last year's pace. For sellers, nearby competition and a strong first impression matter.

The county's median listing price was $459,990, about 1.1% lower than one year earlier. That is an asking-price measure, not a completed-sale price, but it shows that prices were relatively steady while inventory expanded.
market.verificationNote: Source: Realtor.com Economic Research county inventory data for May 2026, released June 3, 2026.

homeownerTip.title: Set up a safer Fourth of July.
homeownerTip.intro: Before the grill is hot or any legal consumer fireworks come out, take a minute to prepare:
items: Keep the grill well away from siding, deck railings, eaves, and overhanging branches.
Never leave a lit grill unattended, and keep children and pets away from the cooking area.
Follow local fireworks laws and label directions, with a responsible adult supervising.
Keep a garden hose or bucket of water ready, and never try to relight a firework that did not work.
homeownerTip.closing: A little preparation keeps the celebration focused on family, food, and fun. For a public fireworks show, leave the setup to the professionals.

localEvent.title: Suwanee Farmers Market
localEvent.intro: If you would like an easy local outing before the holiday celebrations begin, here is one Gwinnett option.
localEvent.copy: The Suwanee Farmers Market is scheduled for Saturday, July 4, from 8:00 AM to noon at Town Center Park. Browse seasonal produce and goods from local farmers and makers, then enjoy a walk around the park.
localEvent.tip: Tip: Check the official City of Suwanee event page before leaving for any weather, parking, or schedule updates.

cartoon.caption: "Snacks, chairs, and a safety plan. We are officially ready."
cartoon.closing: The best celebrations end with nothing more dramatic than an empty dessert plate.
